research.chapter1_title: The Beginning: An Idea Born in the Lab
research.chapter1_body: What if a glove could sense every nuance of a human hand — pressure, angle, movement — and translate that into digital intelligence? That question became the foundation of my Master's thesis at the University of Aizu.
research.chapter2_title: Crafting the Glove: E-Textile Meets Engineering
research.chapter2_body: Starting with raw conductive fabric, I hand-stitched Velostat pressure sensors into each fingertip and palm zone of a standard white glove. Combined with IMU sensors tracking orientation in 3D space, the glove became a complete hand-sensing system.
research.chapter3_title: Intelligence in Action: Solving the Tower of Hanoi
research.chapter3_body: The first challenge was proving the glove could guide complex problem-solving. The Tower of Hanoi — a classic puzzle requiring precise, logical moves — became our test. The glove reads your grip, the desktop UI processes sensor data in real time, and tells you exactly where to place the ring.
research.chapter4_title: Seeing is Believing: Ray-Ban Meta AR Integration
research.chapter4_body: The glasses became the bridge between the glove and the user's mind. Ray-Ban Meta's transparent display lets the system guide hand movements in real time — showing exactly where each finger should go, and how much pressure to apply. It's not just rehabilitation; it's intelligent feedback.
research.chapter5_body: The true power emerges when all three systems work in perfect harmony. The glove senses, the processor understands, and the AR display guides — in real time, with nearly imperceptible latency. Rehabilitation becomes intelligent, adaptive, and deeply humane.
